text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- The 1,500 Norwegian inhabitants on Spitzbergen own a total 1,000 snow scooters, but some are reckless drivers. Deputy District governor Rune Baard Hansen says snow scooter drivers who violate a speed limit of 30 kph in Longyear town will be fined or even sent to prison.
- Two shipyards in Brattvaagen in western Norway have 50 vacancies. The shipyards are trying to recruit workers from the northeastern Finnmark, has the highest unemployment rate in Norway.
- The value of Norwegian fish exports has increased for the eigth year in a row. Also, from 1961 to 1996 the export value has gone up from 7.1 billion crowns to 22.5 billion 1996-crowns.

- In a recent report the EU commission says the minimum cost for removing oil and gas platforms in the North Sea will be 144 billion crowns. It will cost about 40 billion crowns to clean up the Norwegian sector alone.

- Trondheim on New Years Eve starts to celebrate its 1,000-year anniversary with businessmen hoping that a thousand events planned for 1997 will bring extra revenue of several billion crowns to the city.
